facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Control sits with public shareholders, not a sponsor, and no holder is large enough to dominate the board. The four holders above 5% own 33.13% between them, the largest 11.17%, and directors and executive officers as a group 2.42%. Eleven of thirteen directors are independent; the chief executive and the chair are not. Creditors therefore face no sponsor extraction or exit-timing risk, but there is also no controlling holder whose support could be called on in stress. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 219; calculation C5

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Shareholder distributions, not debt-funded transactions, are the main governance risk to creditors. In fiscal 2026 dividends, share repurchases and treasury stock purchases took USD 737.67 million, which is 91.35% of free cash flow of USD 807.52 million, and the share count fell 4.97%. The quarterly dividend of USD 0.28 per share continues and a renewed repurchase plan allows purchases of up to 10% of the public float. Because these payments take nearly all internally generated cash, debt reduction relies on asset sales and cash on hand, not retained free cash flow. Evidence for High would be debt-funded distributions or acquisitions after the strategic review, use of the universal shelf registration filed in December 2025, or a repurchase programme that outruns free cash flow. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is operating momentum and execution on debt. Core revenue grew 2.4% and core cloud revenue 11.2% in the latest quarter, enterprise cloud bookings rose 22.55%, free cash flow rose in the latest quarter, and the company cut debt by USD 607.55 million in fiscal 2026 and completed a refinancing within a day of the quarter-end. facts.label: Company and operating model
facts.text: Open Text supplies data management software to large and regulated organisations, so its credit case rests on how sticky that revenue is. facts.text: Revenue is mostly recurring and well covered for twelve months, but the base is not growing. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Open Text presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring revenue of 80.93% of sales, contracted revenue of USD 4.6 billion, liquidity of USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit and no note maturity before 2028, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking earnings base, an outlook that lowers margin and free cash flow, payouts of 91.35% of free cash flow and an unsettled financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow of USD 807.52 million is generated after interest, taxes and capital expenditure, but most of it is paid out. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the pace of deleveraging, the cost of rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from 2028, the price of the next issue relative to the 6.70% and 7.15% paid in October 2026, and the investor day. The primary downside path is support attrition outrunning cloud growth with margin at the low end of the outlook, lifting net leverage toward 2.91x on current net debt while payouts continue. Further analysis would require pro forma net debt after the October 2026 events, the covenant ratio for 30 September 2026, the executed credit documents, letters of credit issued, a credit rating and a peer set for comparison. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top Risk: support revenue erosion outrunning cloud growth while payouts continue. ## Request

This is the source-readiness assessment of OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 for the credit snapshot pathway. It tests whether the seven supplied issuer documents can support the Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit work requested in this run. It draws no credit conclusion.
## Sources
No earlier module output was supplied to this module. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied documents are enough for a fundamentals-only credit snapshot of Open Text Corporation at 5 November 2026, but not for legal, ratings, market or peer work, so creditors should treat the post-October 2026 capital structure as management-described.

The documents rebuild five consecutive discrete quarters to 30 September 2026, four of which tie to the audited year, and they print debt, covenant, liquidity and outlook disclosure to that date. They end one day before the issuer replaced its USD 1.0 billion secured notes, so the latest balance sheet shows the old debt stack and the new one appears only in notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3
### Key findings

- Each fiscal 2026 quarter ties to its parent period. The first three quarters add to the nine-month revenue printed in the March 2026 quarterly report, the audited year less those nine months equals the fourth-quarter revenue in the latest release, and the four quarterly adjusted EBITDA figures add to the printed full-year figure. Five discrete quarters, from the quarter ended 30 September 2025 (supplied as a comparative) to the quarter ended 30 September 2026, are therefore available.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Every debt instrument is listed with principal and rate at 30 June 2026 and 30 September 2026: five note series, each with its maturity date, and the Acquisition Term Loan. The term loan states a seven-year term from funding but no maturity date. Principal ties to balance-sheet carrying value at both dates, and the USD 750 million revolver had no borrowings at either date.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 268–270; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4; calculation C5

- The latest balance sheet precedes the October 2026 refinancing. On 1 October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500 million of 6.70% secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% secured notes due 2033. On 2 October 2026 it redeemed USD 1.0 billion of 2027 secured notes and purchased and cancelled USD 300 million of 2028 unsecured notes, and the revolver maturity was extended from 19 December 2028 to 1 October 2031, subject to conditions. The terms are stated, but no pro forma balance sheet is given and the cash spent on premium, accrued interest and costs is not quantified.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The financial maintenance covenant the filings describe is a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 4.50x under both the revolver and the term loan. The issuer printed 3.35x at 31 December 2025, 3.02x at 31 March 2026 and 2.75x at 30 June 2026. For 30 September 2026 the quarterly report states compliance only, and the November 2026 release gives a net leverage ratio of 2.55x without defining it. The covenant EBITDA is defined in an agreement that was not supplied and is worded differently from the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, so a leverage figure built from adjusted EBITDA is not the covenant ratio.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2025-12-31_otex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-03-31_otex-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Cash of USD 983.3 million at 30 September 2026 and the undrawn revolver are printed. Letters of credit appear only as a type of guarantee and inside the covenant definitions, with no amount issued under the revolver, so availability net of letters of credit is not established.

- No credit rating level, market price, spread quote, peer set or portfolio input was supplied, and the filings mention ratings only as a risk factor and in forward-looking caveats. Work that needs those inputs cannot draw on this document set.

- The credit agreement, indentures and security documents are listed by reference in the annual report exhibit index but were not supplied. The annual report and the quarterly reports summarise their terms, so those summaries are the only evidence for ranking, guarantees, call terms and covenant definitions, and the terms of the October 2026 notes are set out in the notes to the November 2026 quarterly report, not in executed documents.

- From the first quarter of fiscal 2027 the issuer reports eight product categories instead of seven, and only the quarter ended 30 September 2025 was recast, so category revenue breaks between the annual report and the latest quarter while total revenue is unaffected. Ranges for fiscal 2027 revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow are printed in the annual report and maintained unchanged in the latest quarterly report.

- Ownership is dispersed: the largest holder in the ownership table holds 11.17% of the common shares and no sponsor is named. The chief executive changed on 20 April 2026 after a period under an interim chief executive. Statements are consolidated for Open Text Corporation, and no issuer-level or guarantor-level financial statements are printed, so structural priority rests on the notes' descriptions rather than on entity accounts.

- Leases, pensions, purchase obligations, guarantees and the Canadian tax reassessment dispute are disclosed in the notes. The contractual-obligations tables at both dates print lease, future-lease and purchase amounts apart from debt, so each of those claims sits outside the debt figure.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a pass is that every document is written by the issuer, so debt terms, covenant ratios and the net leverage ratio of 2.55x are management statements that cannot be checked against executed agreements, rating agency views or market prices. A restricted verdict would also be reasonable for any work that needs the post-refinancing capital structure, because only the notes to the latest quarterly report describe it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3

The verdict stays at pass with limitations because the requested work is a fundamentals snapshot, and audited statements, quarterly statements, adjusted EBITDA reconciliations and the debt notes meet its evidence demands. It would move to conditional for legal or recovery work, which needs the executed documents. It would improve if a pro forma balance sheet for 2 October 2026 appeared, and the investor day scheduled for 10 February 2027 may change the strategy and the product-category basis.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54
### Limitations
- No executed credit agreement, indenture or security document is supplied, and the run settings declare none, so terms come from the issuer's own summaries.
- No credit rating, market quote, peer set, portfolio or user assumption is supplied; a blank in the run settings is not treated as zero.
- The latest balance sheet is dated 30 September 2026 and the October 2026 refinancing is described in notes only, with no pro forma balance sheet and no amount for the cash used.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44
- Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not quantified in any document.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 129
- The covenant ratio at 30 September 2026 is not printed; only compliance and an undefined net leverage ratio are stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3
- No issuer-level or guarantor-level financial statements are printed.
- Product-category revenue sits on two bases because only one earlier quarter was recast.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10
- The Acquisition Term Loan maturity date is not printed.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 125

## Findings
### Bottom line

Open Text cut leverage to 3.50x reported EBITDA (2.90x net) at 30 September 2026 from 4.16x (3.40x net) at the 2025 fiscal year-end, with cash interest cover of 5.50x, but progress stalled in the latest quarter.

Last-twelve-months EBITDA fell with revenue and higher special charges, so total leverage rose from 3.41x at the 2026 fiscal year-end. The October 2026 refinancing moved the nearest secured maturity from 2027 to 2031 and 2033, but the cash it used is not stated, so net debt and leverage after it are not established.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44
### Key findings

- Leverage on carrying-value debt over reported EBITDA fell from 4.16x at the 2025 fiscal year-end to 3.41x at the 2026 fiscal year-end, as debt fell by USD 607.55 million and reported EBITDA rose by 10.16%. It then rose to 3.50x on a last-twelve-months basis at 30 September 2026, because last-twelve-months EBITDA is USD 40.13 million below the fiscal 2026 figure while debt barely moved: first-quarter revenue fell 4.00% year on year and special charges were USD 33.29 million against USD 20.14 million. Net leverage moved from 3.40x to 2.85x to 2.90x, so the deleveraging of fiscal 2026 has paused.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 233–234; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Cash interest paid fell from USD 352.38 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 321.69 million in fiscal 2026 and to USD 300.11 million over the last twelve months, which lifted reported EBITDA cover from 4.35x to 5.25x and 5.50x. The fall comes from the term loan, whose interest expense dropped as prepayments cut its floating-rate balance, while interest on the fixed-rate notes did not change; cash received for interest is not netted.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 306; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 269–270; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 273

- Free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditure, was USD 807.52 million in fiscal 2026 against USD 687.40 million in fiscal 2025, a conversion of 47.79% of reported EBITDA. Dividends, share repurchases and treasury purchases took USD 737.67 million, or 91.35% of it, so debt repayment of USD 648.85 million depended on USD 311.91 million of divestiture proceeds and a USD 200.85 million fall in cash. Capital returns compete with deleveraging for the same cash.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 117

- Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 983.29 million of cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolver, before letters of credit that no document quantifies. Before 2028 the only principal falling due is term loan amortisation of USD 35.85 million a year; after 2 October 2026 the nearest note maturity is the 2028 notes, with USD 600 million left after the tender. The revolver maturity was extended to 2031, subject to conditions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 268; calculation C5

- The latest balance sheet precedes the October 2026 refinancing. On 1 October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500 million of 6.70% secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% secured notes due 2033, and on 2 October 2026 it redeemed USD 1.0 billion of 2027 secured notes and cancelled USD 300 million of 2028 unsecured notes. Principal ends USD 300 million lower, and the new coupons of 6.70% and 7.15% straddle the 6.90% coupon on the notes redeemed. The cash paid in premium, accrued interest and costs is not stated, so pro forma net debt and leverage are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C13

- Printed covenant ratios and the figures computed here are different measures. The lenders' ratio was 3.35x at 31 December 2025, 3.02x at 31 March 2026 and 2.75x at 30 June 2026, falling with debt; the last sits between net debt over reported EBITDA at 2.85x and net debt over adjusted EBITDA at 2.53x, and its definition sits in agreements that are not supplied. The release's net leverage ratio of 2.55x at 30 September 2026 equals net debt over last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA computed here, although the release does not define it. Covenant capacity is not inferred.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_otex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-03-31_otex-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C4; calculation C12

- Deferred revenue, a funding float that bears no interest, was USD 1,643.15 million at the 2026 fiscal year-end against USD 1,684.14 million a year earlier and USD 1,529.69 million at 30 September 2026. The first quarter drained USD 116.56 million of cash through deferred revenue, against USD 108.80 million a year earlier, and receivables collections of USD 115.80 million offset it; a shrinking float is a claim on cash that creditors do not see in debt.
Basis: calculation C11; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 233; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

- The statements agree internally: assets equal liabilities plus equity, the cash flows reconcile to the change in cash, the 30 June 2026 balance sheet is identical in the annual and quarterly reports, and the issuer's adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow agree to the figures computed here. Dashes in the source are carried as not supplied, never as zero.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 233–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against reading this as a steady deleveraging credit is the company's own fiscal 2027 outlook: revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 32% to 33%, against 36.3% in fiscal 2026 and 35.8% in the latest quarter. A lower margin on lower revenue cuts EBITDA and lifts leverage unless debt falls faster, and the latest quarter already shows that. It would take a second quarter of rising last-twelve-months EBITDA, or debt falling faster than EBITDA, to restore the fiscal 2026 trend.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C4

The strongest support is the maturity profile: nothing but term loan amortisation falls due before 2028, the revolver is undrawn, and the refinancing removed the nearest secured maturity. What would change the view is evidence of cash used in the refinancing large enough to lift net debt, or a covenant ratio at 30 September 2026 close to the 4.50x maximum, neither of which is printed.
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is derived as income from operations plus depreciation and amortization of intangible assets because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA; a different treatment of other income or special charges would move every ratio.
- Net debt after 2 October 2026 is not established: premium, accrued interest, tender price and costs are not stated and no pro forma capitalisation is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44

- Leverage is built only at 30 June 2025, 30 June 2026 and 30 September 2026; interim dates in between are not constructed, and no balance sheet exists in the documents for 30 June 2024 or 30 September 2025.
- Cash interest is the gross amount paid; interest received is not netted, so cover is conservative.
- The ladder of debt maturities leaves out the term loan balance beyond its current portion because its maturity date is not printed.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 272
- The EBITDA bridge starts from derived reported EBITDA, not from the issuer's own net income start, and carries the non-controlling interest step needed to reach the issuer's figure.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 305

This is the business, ownership and governance fact pack for OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the business model, ownership, transactions, capital allocation and sponsor and governance behaviour from the supplied filings and releases. It makes no recovery, peer or instrument recommendation.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Open Text has no sponsor and a mostly independent board, but it returned 91.35% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow to shareholders while a new chief executive and an open strategic review leave its direction unsettled, so governance risk is Medium.

Documented behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: USD 613.0 million of term loan prepayments from divestiture proceeds and cash, and an October 2026 refinancing that extended maturities, sit beside a portfolio being sold down and a share count cut by 4.97% in a year. No document shows priming, an uptier or another creditor-adverse step, but the legal capacity to distribute is not established because the executed agreements are not supplied.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 219
### Key findings

- Control sits with public shareholders, not a sponsor, and no holder is large enough to dominate the board. The four holders above 5% own 33.13% between them, the largest 11.17%, and directors and executive officers as a group 2.42%. Eleven of thirteen directors are independent; the chief executive and the chair are not. Creditors therefore face no sponsor extraction or exit-timing risk, but there is also no controlling holder whose support could be called on in stress.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 219; calculation C5

- Shareholder distributions, not debt-funded transactions, are the main governance risk to creditors. In fiscal 2026 dividends, share repurchases and treasury stock purchases took USD 737.67 million, which is 91.35% of free cash flow of USD 807.52 million, and the share count fell 4.97%. The quarterly dividend of USD 0.28 per share continues and a renewed repurchase plan allows purchases of up to 10% of the public float. Because these payments take nearly all internally generated cash, debt reduction relies on asset sales and cash on hand, not retained free cash flow.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 310; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C3; calculation C4

- The group is deleveraging by selling businesses, which shrinks the earnings base that supports the debt. It bought Micro Focus for USD 6.2 billion in January 2023, financed in part with new secured debt, sold its Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2,275.0 million in May 2024, and sold two more businesses in fiscal 2026 for USD 313.0 million, using all of it to prepay the term loan; a further USD 300.0 million of prepayment came from cash. Management says it regularly evaluates divestitures, so more sales are likely.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 273; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 299–300; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; calculation C6

- Leadership turnover and an open strategic review lower visibility of financial policy. Both the chief executive and chief financial officer roles were interim for part of fiscal 2026, the chair served as executive chair from August 2025 to June 2026 at a cost of USD 3.1 million, a new chief executive started on 20 April 2026, and an enterprise assessment launched in the fourth quarter is due to report at an investor day on 10 February 2027. Business Optimization Plan charges were USD 96.01 million in fiscal 2026 and USD 127.92 million in fiscal 2025. Capital allocation and portfolio policy may change after that date.

- The operating model is recurring but eroding at the support line. Cloud services and customer support made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue; customer support revenue fell from USD 2,713.30 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 2,287.45 million while cloud revenue grew from USD 1,820.52 million to USD 1,958.55 million. No customer exceeded 10% of receivables and the United States was 49.89% of revenue. Cloud migration is replacing support income, so cash flow is durable but its mix is changing.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 261; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 305; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 239; calculation C1

- Disclosure supports monitoring but is silent on entity-level detail. The covenant maximum and the issuer's ratios, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, the debt terms and the sale of each business are printed, yet there are no guarantor-level statements, no letters of credit amount and no executed agreements, so who can receive value, and what the notes allow, cannot be tested.

- A tax dispute with the Canada Revenue Agency is a claim outside debt that carries no accrual. For fiscal 2012 to 2016 the potential liability for penalties, interest and provincial taxes is about USD 87.4 million; for fiscal 2017 to 2021 the company says an adverse outcome could cut deferred tax assets by up to about USD 470 million, with cash tax over several years, and it has provisionally paid about USD 32.0 million and USD 40.3 million so far. A loss would draw on the same cash that serves debt.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for lower risk is behaviour: the company prepaid USD 613.0 million of its term loan in fiscal 2026, extended its nearest maturities in October 2026, has no history in these documents of exchange offers, priming or waivers, and says its focus is cash generation, debt reduction and capital allocation. That argues for Low. Evidence for High would be debt-funded distributions or acquisitions after the strategic review, use of the universal shelf registration filed in December 2025, or a repurchase programme that outruns free cash flow.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_q4-26pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126

The view moves to Low if the investor day sets a leverage target and ranks debt reduction ahead of repurchases, and to High if the next year shows buybacks or acquisitions financed by new debt. The legal documents, which would show how much value can leave, are the missing evidence.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 126–127
### Limitations

- The legal capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add debt or release guarantees is not established because no executed agreement is supplied, so the Medium level rests on documented behaviour and would move if baskets prove wide or tight.

- The documents show conduct only from fiscal 2023, so the absence of exchange offers, priming or waivers describes these documents, not the company's full history; an earlier episode would raise the risk level.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19

- No sponsor fund, vintage or fee data exist because the company is publicly held; the sponsor assessment is therefore limited to shareholders' conduct and cannot be scored on the nine sponsor dimensions beyond those evidenced.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214

- The sums invested in the strategic funds in which the company holds up to about 19.9% limited partner interests are not stated, so related-party leakage can be described but not sized, and the governance conclusion on conflicts stays qualitative.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 218
- The outcome of the strategic review is not published until the investor day, so any conclusion about future capital allocation could reverse after 10 February 2027.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4

On 1 October 2026, after the latest balance sheet, the company issued USD 500 million of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% senior secured notes due 2033. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Open Text is an adequate credit: recurring software revenue and no note maturity before 2028 protect liquidity, but a shrinking earnings base and payouts taking 91.35% of free cash flow leave creditors relying on asset sales, not retained cash, to cut debt.

Net debt was 2.90x reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026 against 2.85x at the 2026 year-end, so deleveraging has paused, and pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established. The outlook lowers the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32% to 33% from 36.3% and free cash flow to USD 625 million to USD 725 million from USD 807.52 million, which is the main reason leverage rises unless debt falls.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

- The business is a recurring franchise whose core is holding while total revenue shrinks. Cloud services and customer support made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue and contracted revenue not yet recognised was USD 4.6 billion, with 57% due within a year, so revenue visibility is good. The four core product categories, 76.79% of revenue, were flat in constant currency in fiscal 2026 and grew 2.7% in constant currency in the latest quarter, while client support fell 8.99% and licence 7.95%, so total revenue fell 4.00% in the quarter, or 1.7% in constant currency excluding divestitures.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C1; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Reported revenue growth in fiscal 2026 was a currency effect, not recovery. Revenue rose 1.51%, but currency added USD 135.96 million, so revenue fell USD 57.96 million in constant currency, and customer support revenue fell 2.00% as reported and 4.8% excluding currency. The fiscal 2027 outlook expects a further USD 30 million currency drag, so creditors should read the outlook range as a decline in reported revenue of 1.65% at its midpoint.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

- Margin is the swing factor, and the company's own outlook cuts it. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.3% in fiscal 2026 and 35.8% in the latest quarter, yet the outlook of 32% to 33% on revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million implies adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million, 11.88% below fiscal 2026, and an average margin of about 31.47% for the remaining three quarters. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is operating momentum and execution on debt. Core revenue grew 2.4% and core cloud revenue 11.2% in the latest quarter, enterprise cloud bookings rose 22.55%, free cash flow rose in the latest quarter, and the company cut debt by USD 607.55 million in fiscal 2026 and completed a refinancing within a day of the quarter-end. ### Company and operating model

Open Text supplies data management software to large and regulated organisations, so its credit case rests on how sticky that revenue is. Cloud services and customer support, which renew, made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue, enterprise clients contribute about 90% of revenue, no customer exceeded a tenth of receivables, and the United States is 49.89% of revenue with most of the rest in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. That mix supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, but growth now has to come from moving support clients to cloud, which carries a lower gross margin.

The group has changed shape since the Micro Focus acquisition for USD 6.2 billion in January 2023: it sold the Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2,275.0 million in May 2024 and two more businesses for USD 313.0 million in fiscal 2026, and used the proceeds to repay the term loan. The earnings base is smaller and rests on the four core categories, 76.79% of revenue, while the lines that are shrinking or being sold are 23.21%; further disposals are possible after the strategic review, which would shrink the base again.

Financial policy is the weak point: payouts took 91.35% of free cash flow, a repurchase plan of up to 10% of the public float runs to August 2027, a new chief executive started on 20 April 2026, the strategic review reports on 10 February 2027, and no leverage target appears in the documents, so leverage tolerance is not established.

### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is intense and widening. The company names IBM, Microsoft, Oracle and ServiceNow among large rivals, competes with Microsoft while also partnering with it, and says AI has extended competition to platform providers and specialist knowledge platforms, so pricing and renewal terms are contested in every category. New entrants matter mainly through AI: they target the same unstructured-data workloads, which pressures the cloud net renewal rate that already slipped to 94%. Substitutes are the sharpest threat, because the company itself warns that clients may build internal AI alternatives, which would hit licence and support revenue first.

Buyer power is moderate: enterprise clients are about 90% of revenue and support renews annually at their option, which lets them push on price at renewal, but no customer is concentrated enough to threaten cash flow. Supplier power is limited: cloud cost of revenues comprises third-party network usage fees, data centre maintenance and support staff, and the network fees rose USD 6.5 million in fiscal 2026, so supplier pricing is a small drag on the 64% cloud margin, not a credit driver.

The next twelve to twenty-four months look manageable for debt service and uncomfortable for leverage. The realistic downside starts with support attrition outrunning cloud migration. ### Overall credit view

Overall, Open Text presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring revenue of 80.93% of sales, contracted revenue of USD 4.6 billion, liquidity of USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit and no note maturity before 2028, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking earnings base, an outlook that lowers margin and free cash flow, payouts of 91.35% of free cash flow and an unsettled financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow of USD 807.52 million is generated after interest, taxes and capital expenditure, but most of it is paid out. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the pace of deleveraging, the cost of rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from 2028, the price of the next issue relative to the 6.70% and 7.15% paid in October 2026, and the investor day. The primary downside path is support attrition outrunning cloud growth with margin at the low end of the outlook, lifting net leverage toward 2.91x on current net debt while payouts continue. Further analysis would require pro forma net debt after the October 2026 events, the covenant ratio for 30 September 2026, the executed credit documents, letters of credit issued, a credit rating and a peer set for comparison. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top Risk: support revenue erosion outrunning cloud growth while payouts continue.

Proven access to secured funding is the fourth strength: the company issued 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes within a day of the quarter-end and extended its revolver to October 2031, which reduces refinancing risk before 2028 even though its coupons are higher than those on the unsecured notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The earnings base is the first weakness. Fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 1.51% was currency, constant-currency revenue fell USD 57.96 million, the latest quarter fell 4.00%, and the outlook lowers the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32% to 33%; implied adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million is 11.88% below fiscal 2026, so leverage rises unless debt falls.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Payouts are the second weakness: dividends, repurchases and treasury purchases took 91.35% of free cash flow, leaving USD 69.85 million, so debt reduction came from divestitures and cash; at the outlook midpoint of free cash flow, about USD 368.63 million remains after the dividend and amortisation, below the USD 469.31 million spent on repurchases in fiscal 2026.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Refinancing cost and floating-rate exposure are the third weakness: rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from their current coupons to 6.70% would add about USD 80.88 million a year as an illustration, and the term loan, 27.64% of principal after the October 2026 events, costs USD 15.3 million more for every rise of 100 basis points; both slow the fall in interest cost that helped cash flow in fiscal 2026.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86

Unsettled financial policy and information gaps are the fourth weakness: a new chief executive, a strategic review reporting on 10 February 2027, no stated leverage target, no executed credit documents and no unaudited covenant ratio for 30 September 2026 mean creditors cannot yet price how cash will be shared with shareholders.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
